contract_plain_english: For a BLR system solved using either the UFC or UCF BLR LU factorization and then BLR forward and backward substitution, the computed xhat exactly solves a nearby system (A + Delta A)xhat = v + Delta v. In Frobenius norm, the coefficient perturbation is bounded by (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| plus gamma_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| and O(u epsilon), while the right-hand-side perturbation is bounded by gamma_p times ||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||xhat|| plus O(u^2), with c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p and xi_p given by all four cases in Table 1 (PDF pp. 19 and 24-25, printed pp. 969 and 974-975, anchors: Table 1, equations (4.23)-(4.25), and the exact proof expansions).

source_evidence.observation: The theorem states the BLR-system solve, the coefficient-and-right-hand-side backward relation, both perturbation bounds, c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p, and the reference to Table 1 for xi_p.

The proof gives the factorization and triangular-solve perturbations and then composes them exactly as Delta A' = Delta A + Delta L_tilde U_tilde + L_tilde Delta U_tilde + Delta L_tilde Delta U_tilde and Delta v' = Delta v + L_tilde Delta yhat + Delta L_tilde Delta yhat.
Table 1 gives xi_p = 1 for local without recompression, p for global without recompression, p for local with recompression, and p^2/sqrt(6) for global with recompression.
A BLR matrix has p by p blocks of size b by b with n = pb; off-diagonal blocks are approximated in Frobenius norm using local or global low-rank thresholds.

source_evidence.anchor: equation (2.5) and the definition of gamma_k
source_evidence.observation: The floating-point model and gamma notation are fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u, and gamma_k = ku/(1-ku) for ku < 1.
The analysis assumes compression satisfies the low-rank truncation bound while ignoring SVD-rounding error, and assumes u is safely smaller than epsilon.
The paper defines r in Section 4 as the largest off-diagonal block rank of the BLR LU factors; r is induced by the matrix and threshold rather than independently tunable.
The UFC factorization theorem assumes a nonsingular matrix partitioned into p^2 blocks of order b and requires Algorithm 1 to run to completion.
The UCF factorization theorem likewise assumes a nonsingular matrix partitioned into p^2 blocks of order b and requires Algorithm 2 to run to completion.
Each BLR triangular solve introduces both a matrix perturbation bounded using gamma_c and a right-hand-side perturbation bounded using gamma_p.
The paper's qualitative stability interpretation additionally relies on the BLR factor norms not being too large, as expected from a stable LU factorization using, for example, partial pivoting.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The result covers exactly the two BLR LU variants referenced as Algorithm 1, update-factor-compress (UFC), and Algorithm 2, update-compress-factor (UCF), followed in either case by BLR forward and backward substitution; xi_p also depends on whether intermediate recompressions are used (PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, anchor: introduction of UFC and UCF; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, anchor: Algorithm 2; PDF pp. 19 and 24, printed pp. 969 and 974, anchors: Table 1 and Theorem 4.5).
binders: Theorem 4.5 binds a BLR matrix A_tilde in R^(n x n), a right-hand side v in R^n, block parameters p and b with n = pb in the surrounding BLR convention, and a computed solution xhat (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: opening of Theorem 4.5; PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, anchor: n = pb after (2.3)).

L_tilde and U_tilde are the computed BLR LU factors produced by either Algorithm 1 (UFC) or Algorithm 2 (UCF), epsilon is the LR threshold, u is unit roundoff, and r is the largest off-diagonal block rank of those factors (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: Theorem 4.5; PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, anchor: definition of r in Section 4).
conclusions: There are total perturbations Delta A and Delta v such that (A + Delta A)xhat = v + Delta v (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: equation (4.23)).
The coefficient perturbation satisfies ||Delta A|| <= (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_(3c)||L_tilde|| ||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon) (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: equation (4.24)).
The right-hand-side perturbation satisfies ||Delta v|| <= gamma_p (||v|| + ||L_tilde|| ||U_tilde|| ||xhat||) + O(u^2) (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: equation (4.25)).
The constant is c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: line immediately following equation (4.25)).

The four values of xi_p are: 1 for a local threshold without recompressions; p for a global threshold without recompressions; p for a local threshold with recompressions; and p^2/sqrt(6) for a global threshold with recompressions (PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, anchor: Table 1).

Before big-O simplification, if E_A denotes the factorization perturbation, E_L and E_U the two triangular-solve factor perturbations, and e_v and e_y their right-hand-side perturbations, the proof composes the coefficient perturbation exactly as E_A + E_L U_tilde + L_tilde E_U + E_L E_U and the right-hand-side perturbation exactly as e_v + L_tilde e_y + E_L e_y (PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, anchor: the two displayed product expansions in the proof of Theorem 4.5).
constants_and_indexing: p is the number of block rows and block columns, b is the block order, n = pb, and r is the maximum off-diagonal rank among the BLR LU factors (PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, anchor: BLR representation; PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, anchor: definition of r).
The coefficient-rounding index is 3c with c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p; the theorem uses gamma_(3c), not 3 gamma_c (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: equation (4.24) and definition of c).
xi_p changes with both threshold scope and recompression: 1, p, p, and p^2/sqrt(6) in the four Table 1 cases (PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, anchor: Table 1).
No iteration-index offset appears in the final theorem; p enters through gamma_p, c and xi_p (PDF pp. 19 and 24, printed pp. 969 and 974, anchors: Table 1 and equations (4.24)-(4.25)).
definitions_and_conventions: The surrounding BLR convention is a p by p block partition with b by b blocks and total dimension n = pb; off-diagonal blocks are stored in low-rank form (PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, anchor: equations (2.2)-(2.3) and the sentence "and so n = pb").

A local threshold uses beta_ij = ||A_ij||, whereas a global threshold uses beta_ij = ||A|| in the base compression definition ||A_ij - A_tilde_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij (PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, anchor: equation (2.4) and following paragraph).

The proof first has A + E_A = L_tilde U_tilde with ||E_A|| <= (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_c||L_tilde|| ||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon) (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: first displayed equation in the proof of Theorem 4.5).

The two computed triangular solves satisfy (L_tilde + E_L)yhat = v + e_v and (U_tilde + E_U)xhat = yhat + e_y, with ||E_L|| <= gamma_c||L_tilde||, ||E_U|| <= gamma_c||U_tilde||, ||e_v|| <= gamma_p||v||, and ||e_y|| <= gamma_p||yhat|| (PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, anchor: first two displayed systems in the proof).

The proof uses primed total perturbations to distinguish them from the factorization and solve perturbations, after which the theorem presents the totals under the unprimed names Delta A and Delta v (PDF pp. 24-25, printed pp. 974-975, anchors: equation (4.23) and the final two displays of the proof).
error_notions: Equation (4.23) is a normwise backward relation allowing simultaneous perturbations of the coefficient matrix and right-hand side (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: equation (4.23)).
Equations (4.24) and (4.25) are absolute perturbation bounds, not a single normalized relative backward-error formula (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchors: equations (4.24)-(4.25)).

The coefficient bound contains both a truncation term xi_p epsilon ||A|| and floating-point terms involving gamma_p and gamma_(3c); the right-hand-side bound depends additionally on ||xhat|| and the computed factor norms (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchors: equations (4.24)-(4.25)).
exceptional_values: The invoked factorization results require the algorithms to run to completion, excluding breakdown of the required LU and triangular solves (PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, anchor: Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, anchor: Theorem 4.3).
The gamma quantities require pu < 1 and 3cu < 1 (PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, anchor: definition of gamma_k; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: Theorem 4.5).
No explicit NaN, infinity, overflow or underflow behavior is included; these cases lie outside the stated standard relative-error model (PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, anchor: equation (2.5)).
higher_order_terms: The coefficient perturbation retains an O(u epsilon) term and the right-hand-side perturbation retains an O(u^2) term; neither is asserted to be zero (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchors: equations (4.24)-(4.25)).

The exact coefficient composition includes the product E_L E_U, and the exact right-hand-side composition includes E_L e_y; these products precede the higher-order simplification (PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, anchor: exact product expansions in the proof).
The constants hidden in O(u epsilon) and O(u^2) are not specified in Theorem 4.5 (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchors: equations (4.24)-(4.25)).
hypotheses: The linear system written in the theorem as A_tilde x = v is solved through the two triangular systems L_tilde y = v followed by U_tilde x = y (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: conditional clause in Theorem 4.5).
The factors must be computed by either Algorithm 1 or Algorithm 2 (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: phrase "computed by either Algorithm 1 or 2").

Through the invoked Theorems 4.2 and 4.3, the matrix is nonsingular, is partitioned into p^2 blocks of order b, and the selected factorization algorithm runs to completion (PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, anchor: Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, anchor: Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: proof invoking those theorems).
The inherited analysis assumes the low-rank truncation model and u safely smaller than epsilon (PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, anchor: Assumption 2.1 and following paragraph).
implicit_context: Theorems 4.2 and 4.3 supply the nonsingularity and run-to-completion conditions that Theorem 4.5 does not restate explicitly (PDF pp. 19, 21 and 24, printed pp. 969, 971 and 974, anchors: Theorems 4.2, 4.3 and the proof of Theorem 4.5).

The formal bounds retain ||L_tilde|| ||U_tilde||; the paper's stronger prose interpretation as backward stability assumes these factor norms are controlled, for example by a stable pivoting scheme (PDF p. 18, printed p. 968, anchor: discussion following Corollary 4.1).

The result combines low-rank truncation error governed by epsilon with floating-point error governed by u; it does not assert that the u-dependent terms vanish (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchors: equations (4.24)-(4.25)).
norms: All unsubscripted norms in Theorem 4.5 are Frobenius norms under the paper-wide convention; vector instances are Euclidean norms (PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, anchor: paragraph defining the unsubscripted Frobenius norm).
The bounds are normwise and contain ||L_tilde|| ||U_tilde|| rather than componentwise growth factors (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchors: equations (4.24)-(4.25)).
numerical_model: Arithmetic follows fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u, for the four elementary operations (PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, anchor: equation (2.5)).

gamma_k = ku/(1-ku) for ku < 1, so the displayed gamma_p and gamma_(3c) bounds require pu < 1 and 3cu < 1; noninteger gamma indices are allowed (PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, anchor: gamma definition and following sentence; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: equations (4.24)-(4.25)).

The analysis assumes u is safely smaller than epsilon and ignores additional rounding in the truncated-SVD compression model (PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, anchor: Assumption 2.1 and following paragraph).

undebatable_constraints: The solve must use L_tilde y = v followed by U_tilde x = y, with factors produced by Algorithm 1 or 2 (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: hypothesis of Theorem 4.5).
The conclusion must permit perturbations to both A and v and retain (A + Delta A)xhat = v + Delta v (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: equation (4.23)).
The coefficient bound is ||Delta A|| <= (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_(3c)||L_tilde|| ||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon) (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: equation (4.24)).
The right-hand-side bound is ||Delta v|| <= gamma_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde|| ||U_tilde|| ||xhat||) + O(u^2) (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: equation (4.25)).
The exact perturbation composition must retain all four coefficient terms and all three right-hand-side terms shown in the proof (PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, anchor: exact product expansions).
The constant is c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p (PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, anchor: line after (4.25)).
The four xi_p values and their threshold/recompression cases must be preserved exactly as in Table 1 (PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, anchor: Table 1).
All error norms are Frobenius norms under the paper-wide convention (PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, anchor: definition of the unsubscripted norm).
